newsitem.title: UK: IPE, NYMEX confirm in talks on trading link-up.
newsitem.headline: IPE, NYMEX confirm in talks on trading link-up.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) and the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) confirmed on Thursday they are considering ways of developing a joint electronic trading system among other areas of cooperation.
"We are going to look at ways of having a common system for the trading out of hours of both NYMEX and IPE contracts," said Richard Ward, head of product development at the IPE.
Ward told a press conference detailed discussion would start in the next few weeks "with a target of reaching an official agreement in the third quarter".

Apart from exploring the possibility of a joint out-of-hours trading platform which could list NYMEX and IPE contracts, both exchanges were investigating the benefits of cross-margining, systems cooperation and joint marketing initiatives.

Ward said the IPE remained committed to developing its Brent contract via a two-year old link-up with the Singapore Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) and rejected suggestions that it was aiming to drop its Asian partner.
"We want the SIMEX agreement to succeed. We didn't enter into it halfheartedly," Ward said.

"Clearly we need to have the agreement of all the interested parties to be able to progress this -- we do not want to end up with a damaged relationship or adversarial relationship with any exchange around the world," he said
SIMEX would be involved in the NYMEX-IPE discussions over the coming months, he added.

Ward was unable to estimate the potential cost savings to members but said there could be significant benefits in cross-margining -- reducing the amount of cash traders have to pay up front for spread trades between the exchanges contracts -- and in reduced systems costs.
"We have entered into this with the belief that there are real benefits to be accrued for the members and therefore for the customers," he said.
"If we're able to have one common platform trading both IPE and NYMEX contracts then certainly from a members perspective they only need one system on their desks," he added.
The new electronic trading system for the IPE's natural gas contract costs about 15,000 sterling, industry sources said.
